criticalFindings.title: All artifact SHA256 digests are incorrect - violates CON-1 constraint
criticalFindings.description: Every artifact file (SC-1, SC-2, SC-3, CON-1, UNK-1, TC-1, TC-2) has a SHA256 digest that does not match the documented digest in the formalization. This is a fundamental violation of CON-1 which requires 'All material transport between define-product-intent desk components must use content address referencing' with 'SHA256 content digests'.
criticalFindings.impact: The entire content address transport mechanism is broken. Without correct SHA256 digests, downstream components cannot verify intent integrity or resolve content to exact artifact states. This is a complete failure of the formalization's core architectural principle.

criticalFindings.title: Workspace summary mismatch - protocol vs formalization disagreement
criticalFindings.description: The protocol message indicates 'workspace: 1 accepted upstream revisions travel by content address' but the formalization JSON states 'workspaceSummary: 0 accepted upstream revisions travel by content address'. This is a fundamental disagreement about the workspace state that must be resolved before acceptance.

evidence.value: 1 accepted upstream revisions travel by content address

criticalFindings.impact: The formalization may be based on incorrect workspace assumptions. If there is actually 1 accepted upstream revision, the entire formalization needs to account for this existing state.

criticalFindings.title: Trace relationships reference incorrect digests - complete trace failure
criticalFindings.description: The formalization trace JSON references SHA256 digests that don't match the actual file contents. Since all artifact digests are incorrect, the entire trace graph is referencing non-existent content states. The trace shows '100% coverage' but this is meaningless when the references are wrong.
criticalFindings.impact: The trace graph cannot be used for verification or dependency tracking when all digest references are incorrect. Downstream components cannot follow derivation chains or resolve content.

criticalFindings.title: Protocol message violates content address transport requirements
criticalFindings.description: The protocol message itself uses SHA256 digests as artifact identifiers (e.g., 'sha256:fbe292e862ab174b29de15cbbf85b34e4211b3a0e508fd39245015c9ea12b180') rather than proper content address transport. Per CON-1, 'Product intent identity is determined solely by cryptographic content digest, never by mutable identifiers', but the protocol is using full SHA256 hashes with 'sha256:' prefix instead of proper content addressing.
criticalFindings.impact: The protocol message itself demonstrates misunderstanding of content address transport, which suggests the formalization may have similar fundamental issues.

secondaryFindings.title: Upstream revision reference cannot be verified
secondaryFindings.description: The protocol message references 'upstream-accepted[0] sha256:15ed5b0ef55569e59e3ecd873c22fdc22067cd882be6ae84d1c40a95a23f5c1e' but no corresponding file exists. This cannot be verified and may indicate protocol confusion.
secondaryFindings.impact: Unclear whether there is actually an accepted upstream revision that should influence this formalization.

secondaryFindings.title: Acceptance criteria cannot be verified given digest failures
secondaryFindings.description: The formalization claims all acceptance criteria are met (marked with ✅ in TC-1 and TC-2), but given the critical digest failures, criteria like 'All product intent artifacts are content-addressed' and 'Content digest verification at each transport boundary' cannot be verified.
secondaryFindings.impact: The formalization's verification claims are unsubstantiated.

recommendation: REJECT formalization for complete resubmission. The content address integrity failures are fundamental and cannot be partially addressed. The entire formalization must be corrected with proper SHA256 digests before it can be considered for acceptance.
reviewerNotes: This formalization demonstrates good architectural understanding and proper structure, but the content address implementation is completely broken. Every artifact has an incorrect SHA256 digest, which violates the core constraint (CON-1) and makes the entire trace graph unusable. The workspace summary disagreement adds additional uncertainty. The formalization needs to be completely corrected with proper cryptographic content addressing before resubmission.
